tasks.title: Rules library and test project
tasks.description: A .NET solution in the repo containing a plain C# rules library, which does not depend on Godot or on rendering, and a test project for it. Every later port task builds into these. Both sit beside the TypeScript build without touching it.
acceptance_criteria: `dotnet test` builds the rules library and its test project and runs successfully
The rules library builds with no reference to Godot or rendering code, and adding one fails the build
`npm run verify` and `npm run dev` work exactly as before, and no TypeScript build file is changed
`dotnet test` run from the repo root finds and runs the test project through `AncientOrder.sln`
Adding any PackageReference, ProjectReference, or assembly Reference to `AncientOrder.Rules.csproj` fails its build with a message saying the rules library must stay dependency-free
A nullable warning or a recommended-level analyzer warning in a rules project fails the build
`./verify.ps1` runs the formatting check, the solution build, and the tests, and exits non-zero if any step fails
tasks.technical_approach: A classic `AncientOrder.sln` at the repo root holds the C# projects: `rules/AncientOrder.Rules` (the rules library, net10.0, zero dependencies), `rules/AncientOrder.Rules.Tests` (xUnit v3 on Microsoft.Testing.Platform), and later the Godot project `godot/AncientOrder.csproj` (added by T13). `global.json` pins the .NET 10 SDK and selects the Microsoft.Testing.Platform runner for `dotnet test`. `rules/Directory.Build.props` applies only to projects under `rules/`: nullable enabled, latest C#, implicit usings, AnalysisLevel latest-Recommended, warnings as errors. A root `.editorconfig` has only `[*.cs]` sections, so the TypeScript tooling and Prettier are unaffected. The library enforces its independence twice: an MSBuild target in its csproj errors if any non-implicit PackageReference, ProjectReference, or Reference appears, and an architecture test asserts the compiled assembly references only framework assemblies (none starting with "Godot"). This task also lays down the shared conventions every rules task follows (see producer_notes) and their small shared types in `Common/`. Two dependency-free guards keep the conventions honest: `.editorconfig` raises the culture-sensitive string analyzers (CA1304, CA1305, CA1307, CA1309, CA1310, CA1311) to errors for `rules/**.cs`, and a metadata-scan test (System.Reflection.Metadata, part of the framework) fails if the compiled rules assembly references a banned API (see producer_notes). The default roll source is the library's own seeded generator (xoshiro256**, seeded through SplitMix64), because Microsoft does not guarantee `System.Random`'s sequence across .NET versions; a golden-sequence test pins its exact output. `verify.ps1` at the root is the one command: `dotnet format --verify-no-changes`, `dotnet build AncientOrder.sln`, `dotnet test`; T13 appends the Godot import and headless smoke steps. The TypeScript build is not touched: every TS config is scoped to `src/` and `tests/`; only `.gitignore` gains the C# and Godot build folders.
tasks.interfaces: Produces the solution, the two rules projects, and the shared `Common` types every engine task builds on: `Result<T>` (success value or `RuleError`), `RuleError(ErrorCode Code, string Message, ImmutableArray<RuleErrorDetail> Details)` with `RuleErrorDetail(string Path, string Message)` (e.g. path `actions/1` for a rejected order), `ErrorCode` (mirrors the live TS codes in `src/types/index.ts` ErrorCodes: GAME_NOT_FOUND, INVALID_SLOT, SAVE_NOT_FOUND, NPC_NOT_FOUND, TEAM_COMPOSITION_INVALID, VALIDATION_ERROR, INTERNAL_ERROR, NO_ACTIVE_COMBAT, COMBAT_INVALID_DECLARATION, ENCOUNTER_NOT_FOUND, COMBAT_ALREADY_ACTIVE, STORAGE_ERROR; the dialogue and narrative codes of the retired engines and the unused INVALID_PERSONALITY_ADJUSTMENT are not carried), `IRollSource` (returns a double in [0,20) like the TS `rollFn`, which is `Math.random() * 20`; default `SeededRolls`: xoshiro256** seeded by SplitMix64, roll = (next >> 11) * 2^-53 * 20), `DiceState` (the generator's four 64-bit words as an immutable, saveable record; `DiceState.FromSeed(ulong)`; `SeededRolls.FromState(DiceState)` and `.State` let a fight carry its dice and resume them exactly after a save), `ISeedSource` (new fight seeds; default `SystemSeedSource` uses `RandomNumberGenerator`), `IIdSource` (new ids; `GuidIdSource` default), and `JsMath` (JS-identical rounding). The clock is .NET's `TimeProvider` (System by default; `FakeTimeProvider` in tests). Rules functions take `now`, rolls, and ids as parameters; only the session (T9) holds the sources. Tests get `FixedRolls` (a scripted roll sequence) and `StateAssert.Equivalent` (compares two states by their JSON form with `JsonNode.DeepEquals`, which ignores object property order, since records holding immutable collections don't compare by value and lookup maps have no fixed order).

design_decisions.decision: Target .NET 10 for every C# project
design_decisions.rationale: Spike: Godot 4.7.2 built and ran a net10.0 game project that references a net10.0 library, headless, with the exit code propagating. .NET 8 support ends Nov 2026 and the machine has no .NET 8 runtime. Desktop export with net10 is unverified until export templates are installed; retargeting is a one-property change.

design_decisions.decision: Classic AncientOrder.sln, not .slnx
design_decisions.rationale: Godot builds the csproj directly and there is no evidence it reads .slnx; a classic solution also stops the Godot editor from generating a second one.

design_decisions.decision: Rules library has zero dependencies, enforced by a build guard and an architecture test
design_decisions.rationale: ADR-063: the rules are independent of Godot and rendering. A guard that fails the build catches it before any test runs.

design_decisions.decision: Immutable sealed records; order is always explicit: ImmutableArray where order matters, ImmutableDictionary for lookup only and never iterated, no sorted dictionaries
design_decisions.rationale: Designer-approved after research (2026-10-28). A spike showed System.Text.Json reloads an ImmutableSortedDictionary with the culture-sensitive default comparer, so key order changed with the OS language and re-saves differed. The TypeScript iterates objects in insertion order (Elena, Lars, Kade), which id-sorted order would silently change, and order matters (e.g. group damage is summed in insertion order and double addition is order-sensitive).

design_decisions.decision: Culture-sensitive string APIs are build errors in the rules
design_decisions.rationale: Same root cause as the sorted-map finding; catches the bug class at compile time.

design_decisions.decision: Refusals as Result<T> values; only real bugs throw, and the session turns them into INTERNAL_ERROR
design_decisions.rationale: Carries ADR-057's results-as-values into the rules themselves.

design_decisions.decision: Rolls, clock, and ids are handed in (IRollSource, TimeProvider, IIdSource)
design_decisions.rationale: Any outcome can be reproduced exactly from its rolls, live fights included.

design_decisions.decision: The library's own seeded generator (xoshiro256** via SplitMix64), not System.Random
design_decisions.rationale: Designer-approved after research (2026-10-28): Microsoft's docs say seeded System.Random sequences may differ between .NET versions, which would break replays after an upgrade. Integer-only state is exactly reproducible; a golden test pins it.

design_decisions.decision: Keep double arithmetic with JS-identical rounding (halves up), stable sorts, and the same order of operations; ban transcendental and fused math in the rules
design_decisions.rationale: Designer-approved after research (2026-10-28). Integer or fixed-point math (suggested by research) would change results throughout combat and break parity. IEEE 754 requires + - * / to be correctly rounded, and the engine uses only those plus floor, round, min, max (verified by grep), so results match the TypeScript to the last digit. Whether RyuJIT ever fuses a*b+c implicitly could not be sourced; the carried-over tests pin exact values and would catch it.

design_decisions.decision: xUnit v3 on Microsoft.Testing.Platform, one C# test file per TypeScript test file with the same test names
design_decisions.rationale: Lets the port record account for every TypeScript test one-to-one.

design_decisions.decision: verify.ps1 as the single check
design_decisions.rationale: Mirrors `npm run verify`: formatting plus nullable and analyzer warnings as errors is the C# equivalent of typecheck plus lint.

tasks.producer_notes: Conventions every rules task (T2–T12) follows: (1) Types are `sealed record`s with init-only properties; updates use `with` and never mutate. Order is always explicit: use `ImmutableArray<T>` wherever order matters; use `ImmutableDictionary<string,T>` (built with `StringComparer.Ordinal`) for lookup only and never iterate it; never use `ImmutableSortedDictionary` or `SortedDictionary`. When something must be walked in order, walk an explicit ordered list (for characters, the catalog's content order) and look values up by id. (2) Expected refusals return `Result<T>.Fail(new RuleError(code, message))` with the same code and message text as the TypeScript; never throw for them. (3) No `Random`, `DateTime.Now`, `DateTimeOffset.UtcNow`, or `Guid.NewGuid()` inside rules functions: take an `IRollSource`, a `long now` (Unix ms, as TS `Date.now()`), or an `IIdSource`. (4) Use `JsMath.Round` wherever the TypeScript uses `Math.round`; never `Math.Round` (banker's rounding) or `MidpointRounding.ToPositiveInfinity` (that is directed rounding, not round-half-up). (5) Sorts must be stable: use `OrderBy`/`ThenBy`, never `List.Sort`/`Array.Sort`. (6) Keep double arithmetic in the same order as the TypeScript expression. (7) Where TS iterates `Object.values`/`Object.keys`, iterate in the same order the TS object had (insertion order); state that order explicitly in each task. (8) Banned in the rules assembly, enforced by BannedApiTests: `System.Random`; `DateTime.Now`/`UtcNow`/`Today`, `DateTimeOffset.Now`/`UtcNow`; `Guid.NewGuid`; `Math.Round` and `MathF.*`; `Math.Pow`, `Exp`, `Log*`, `Sqrt`, `Cbrt`, trig and hyperbolic functions, `FusedMultiplyAdd`, `ScaleB`; `List<T>.Sort`, `Array.Sort`, `ImmutableArray<T>.Sort`; anything in `System.Numerics.Vector*` or `System.Runtime.Intrinsics`; `ImmutableSortedDictionary`/`SortedDictionary`. JsMath may use `Math.Floor`. Allowlist (the only places nondeterminism may enter): `GuidIdSource` may call `Guid.NewGuid`, and `SystemSeedSource` may call `RandomNumberGenerator`; BannedApiTests also bans `RandomNumberGenerator` everywhere else. (9) Save files never serialize rules state directly; T11 maps state to its own save-format records. Namespaces: `AncientOrder.Rules.{Common,Personality,State,Party,Combat,Combat.Ai,Session,Saves}`. The guard target must ignore items with `IsImplicitlyDefined == true` (the SDK adds some for AOT analysis). Do not edit any file under `src/`, `tests/`, or the TS configs, or `package.json`. Test projects may suppress analyzer rules that clash with xUnit naming (such as CA1707) in their own csproj only.

acceptance_criteria: A personality always has the six traits, each between 5% and 35%, summing to 100%, and anything else is reported invalid
Adjusting a personality gives the same resulting values as the TypeScript build for the same inputs, unless the designer changed it on purpose
A new player starts with the same default personality as today, unless the designer changed it on purpose
A personality is never changed in place; every adjustment produces a new one
Every adjusted personality sums to 100 within 0.001 and keeps every trait within 5–35, proven by a randomized test of at least 100,000 adjustments from a fixed seed

Wherever the TypeScript result already summed to 100, the C# result is identical to the last digit

tasks.technical_approach: A direct port of `src/personality/personalitySystem.ts` into `AncientOrder.Rules.Personality`, with one deliberate fix. `Trait` is an enum in the TypeScript PERSONALITY_TRAITS order (Patience, Empathy, Cunning, Logic, Kindness, Charisma); that order is load-bearing (tie-breaks and iteration) and `PersonalityRules.Traits` exposes it as an ImmutableArray. `Personality` is a sealed record with one double per trait plus an indexer by `Trait`. `PersonalityRules` holds the constants (min 5, max 35, total 100, tolerance 0.01, correction threshold 0.001, 10 redistribution passes) and the functions `CreateDefault()`, `Sum(p)`, `Validate(p)`, and `Adjust(current, adjustment)`. `Adjust` keeps the three-pass algorithm exactly (apply and clamp each delta present, a zero delta still counting as adjusted; distribute the difference proportionally over unadjusted traits, or all six when none are unadjusted; up to 10 even-split passes over traits with headroom until |residual| <= 0.01; round each trait to 2 decimals with JsMath). Fix: the final micro-correction goes to the largest trait that can take it and stay within 5–35 after 2-decimal rounding (first in trait order on ties), instead of always the largest trait. When the largest trait can take it, the result is identical to today. Verified against the TypeScript over 800,000 random adjustments: the TS left 5.5% of large shifts off by 0.01 (sum 99.99 or 100.01, about two-thirds of them rejected by its own validity check, which makes the save refuse); the fix leaves none, and it changes no result whose sum was already 100.
tasks.interfaces: Produces `Trait`, `Personality`, `PersonalityAdjustment` (a record wrapping an `ImmutableDictionary<Trait,double>` of deltas; lookup only), `PersonalityValidation(bool Valid, ImmutableArray<string> Errors)`, and `PersonalityRules` (CreateDefault, Sum, Validate, Adjust, Traits, constants). Consumed by T3 (player personality, character catalog validation, starting personality), T4 (synergy reads trait values in trait order), T9 (the session's adjustment input checks: at least one key, trait keys only, finite numbers), and T11 (save checks reuse Validate).

design_decisions.decision: Fix the micro-correction: the leftover goes to the largest trait that can take it within 5–35
design_decisions.rationale: Designer decision 2026-10-28. Today a trait capped at 35 swallows the correction and the total stays at 99.99, so saving is refused. Proven by running both versions over 800,000 adjustments.

design_decisions.decision: Keep everything else as today: default personality with charisma 16.65, a zero delta counts as adjusted, tolerance 0.01 for validity, 10 passes
design_decisions.rationale: No reason to change; parity is the default. The default's comment ('all equal') is wrong, not the value: six traits at 16.67 would total 100.02.

tasks.producer_notes: Port line by line from `src/personality/personalitySystem.ts` (adjustPersonality at lines 124–210); keep the order of every double operation, iterate traits in `PersonalityRules.Traits` order, use JsMath.Round for the 2-decimal rounding (`JsMath.Round(x * 100) / 100`). Micro-correction fix: candidates are traits whose `JsMath.Round((value + diff) * 100) / 100` lies within [5, 35]; pick the largest value among candidates, first in trait order on ties; if no candidate exists (not reachable in practice), fall back to today's behavior. Keep the final clamp. Validate's error messages match the TypeScript text. No input validation inside Adjust (the session checks input, as today).

tasks.technical_approach: Characters are split into what never changes and what changes in play, with one module owning character logic. (1) Content: `GameContent` is the read-only bundle the session plays from, created through `GameContent.Create(...)`, which validates and returns `Result<GameContent>`. This task gives it `Settings` (`GameSettings`: PlayerName, optional StartingPersonality, LineupSize) and `Characters` (`CharacterCatalog`); T4 adds `Synergy`, T6 adds the AI profiles, and T8 adds the encounters, each extending `GameContent` and its validation. Sprint 7's content packs will fill this same record from files. (2) `CharacterCatalog` holds `CharacterDefinition`s (Id, Name, ArchetypeId, fixed Personality, StartingAffection, StartingTrust, optional `Combat`) in content order (`ImmutableArray`, which is the order every listing and every walk uses) plus a `FrozenDictionary` index by id (ordinal). `CombatProfile` (Rank, Stamina, Power, Speed, ElementalPath, AscensionLevel defaulting to 0) gives a character's fighting stats; a character without one never fights. `GameSettings` also gains an optional `PlayerCombat` profile; without it the player character does not fight (T8). Reaction skills are not part of the profile, because the player's side derives them from reaction progress (ADR-054). Definitions never change during play (ADR-003). Join conditions from Sprint 7's shared condition system are added when that system arrives; no speculative fields now. (3) `GameState` is the per-playthrough record: `Player` (`PlayerCharacter`: Id, Name, Personality), `Characters` (`ImmutableDictionary<string, CharacterState>`, lookup only; CharacterState holds Affection and Trust), `Lineup` (`ImmutableArray<string>`), `Combat` (`CombatState?`, from T5), `ReactionProgress` (from T5, same shape as the TypeScript record keyed by combatant id), and `Timestamp` (Unix ms). Dropped: currentDialogueNode, conversationLog, narrativeState, the never-written saveSlot, and the dialogue and scene types. (4) `CharacterRules` is the characters module, and the only code that reads or changes characters. Queries: `Get(content, state, id)` returns a `CharacterView` (definition and state combined) or NPC_NOT_FOUND; `All(content, state)` returns views in catalog order; `InLineup(content, state)` returns views in lineup order. Updates: `ChangeAffection`, `ChangeTrust`, and `ChangeRelationship` add the change and clamp to [−100, 100] exactly as the TypeScript does, returning `Result<GameState>`, and refuse an unknown id with NPC_NOT_FOUND (today that is a silent no-op). (5) `GameStateUpdates` holds the remaining updaters: `NewGame(content, playerId, now)`, `SetPlayerPersonality`, `AdjustPlayerPersonality` (through T2's Adjust), and `WithCombat`. Every successful update sets `Timestamp = now`; a refusal changes nothing. The session (T9) is the only caller from outside the library.

Consumed by T4 (lineup validation against the catalog; synergy reads the player and lineup personalities through CharacterRules.InLineup), T8 (fight setup reads the player and lineup), T9 (session operations and the new-game call: the session supplies `player_<id from IIdSource>` and `now` from TimeProvider), and T11 (saves store GameState's changing parts and pair them with the current catalog on load).

tasks.technical_approach: Two parts in `AncientOrder.Rules.Party`, plus a small general stat-bonus pipeline. (1) Lineup: `LineupRules.Set(content, state, ImmutableArray<string> ids, now)` returns `Result<GameState>` and refuses, in the TypeScript order, with TEAM_COMPOSITION_INVALID: combat active ('Cannot change team during combat'), wrong size ("Team must contain exactly {N} NPCs"), unknown id ('Invalid NPC ID: {id}', checked against the catalog), a character with no combat stats (new: '{id} has no combat stats', since the lineup is who fights, per T8), duplicate ('Duplicate NPC ID: {id}', the first repeated id). The narrative-scene refusal is dropped with the narrative state. The lineup can never be cleared back to empty, as today. (2) Synergy: bonuses are content. `SynergyBonusDefinition` = Name, Rule (`Coverage`, today's Well Rounded scoring; `Alignment`, today's Bond scoring), Threshold, Stat, Step, Value; `SynergySettings` = the bonuses in priority order plus `Resolution` (`BestOnly` | `AllThatQualify`); `GameContent` gains `Synergy`. `SynergyCalculator.Evaluate(settings, player, companions)` scores each bonus with today's math. Coverage: the pool is player plus companions, the max per trait in trait order, any max under the threshold fails, quality = sum of maxes / (6 × threshold). Alignment: per companion in the order given, its top two traits by value (stable: trait order on ties); ratio = (player's two) / (companion's two), skipping a zero sum; best ratio over companions; qualifies at best ≥ threshold / 100; quality = best ratio. BestOnly returns the highest quality, with ties going to the earlier bonus; AllThatQualify returns all qualifying bonuses in content order. `Synergy.Current(content, state)` feeds the player and `CharacterRules.InLineup` (lineup order) into Evaluate, so the bonus always reflects the current personality and lineup and is never stored. The test content mirrors today exactly: Well Rounded (Coverage, 25, Power, Multiply, 1.10), Bond (Alignment, 80, Speed, Multiply, 1.10), BestOnly.

tasks.technical_approach: A port of `declaration.ts`, `pipeline.ts`, `counterChain.ts`, `groupAction.ts`, and `roundManager.ts` into `AncientOrder.Rules.Combat`, with the approved changes. `RoundManager.RunRound(combatState, playerOrders, archetypes)` draws every roll from the fight's own dice (`SeededRolls.FromState(combatState.Dice)`) and returns the new CombatState with `Dice` advanced, so a fight resumed from a save replays the same luck. The overload `RunRound(combatState, playerOrders, archetypes, IRollSource rolls)` is the test seam: it uses the given rolls and leaves `Dice` unchanged. Both keep today's phases in order. P1: `EnemyDecisions.Decide` for each living enemy in enemy-party order, with `GroupActionsEnabled = false`, so enemies never choose GROUP; no catch-all. P2 (the discarded visual info) is not ported. P3: player orders validated in order by `Declarations.Validate`, which keeps today's checks and order (fighter exists and isn't KO; known type; target rules per type; stamina > 0; SPECIAL needs energy > 0; GROUP needs every living ally at maxEnergy, otherwise it falls back to ATTACK on the same target), plus the new rule that a second order for a fighter already holding one is rejected. An accepted GROUP removes the living allies' orders, as today. P4: the queue is enemy actions then player actions, ordered by `Pipeline.Order`: priority (GROUP 0, DEFEND 1, ATTACK/SPECIAL 2, EVADE 3), then effective speed descending (GROUP uses its team's average non-KO speed), then the new tie rule. Every action sharing its priority and speed with another draws one roll, in queue order, before resolution; higher rolls go first; equal rolls keep queue order. The sort is stable. P5: actions resolve one by one with today's roll order per attack: Rank KO (if eligible), Blindside (if eligible), defense (always), Crushing Blow (if Block and action power > target power), then one roll per counter exchange; GROUP takes one roll. Changes inside resolution: (a) Crushing Blow uses action power (`rawDamage`, the spreadsheet's O) for eligibility and threshold; (b) the DEFEND intercept skips knocked-out interceptors; (c) GROUP resolves its forced Block against `Defense.EffectiveReactionSkills(target)`. Post-round, victory and defeat are checked as today (defeat wins when all players are KO), and the round record is `RoundResult(Round, Actions, Snapshot)`, where Snapshot is the end-of-round CombatState with an empty RoundHistory. `ActionResult` gains `CounterExchanges` (each exchange's attacker, defender, defense, outcome, damage) and `EvadeRecovery` (stamina regained). Outcomes are otherwise exactly today's. KO is the explicit flag (T5).

It is constructed with a `GameContent` and `GameSessionOptions` (`TimeProvider`, System by default; `IIdSource`; `ISeedSource`; `Action<Exception>? OnListenerError`; T12 adds the save store). It holds one `SessionSnapshot` record: Version (long), Game (`GameState?`), PendingOrders (`ImmutableArray<CombatAction>`), LastCombatOutcome (`CombatOutcome?`: status and round), Synergy (`ImmutableArray<SynergyResult>`, from `Synergy.Current`, empty without a game). tasks.technical_approach: A fresh save format in `AncientOrder.Rules.Saves`, carrying over ADR-058's envelope, versioning, and never-throwing parse, with its own records separate from the rules state. (1) Format records (`Saves/Format/`): `SaveEnvelope` {format 'ancient-order-save', version 1, kind 'manual', slot, savedAt (Unix ms), playerName, game}; `SavedGame` {timestamp, player {id, name, personality}, characters [{id, affection, trust}] in catalog order, lineup [ids], reactionProgress [{id, block, dodge, parry}] sorted by id (ordinal), combat (a full mirror of CombatState, including its dice as four unsigned integers, or null)}. Every collection is a JSON array in a defined order (no maps), enums are written as strings, property names are camelCase, and the JSON is indented. Serialization uses a System.Text.Json source-generated context (`SaveJsonContext`). (2) Writing: `SaveFormat.Write(slot, kind, game, now)` checks the game the way today's save does (VALIDATION_ERROR 'Game state is invalid: …'), maps it to the format records, serializes it to UTF-8, and refuses anything over 2,000,000 bytes ('Save is too large to write ({n} bytes, limit 2000000)'). (3) Reading: `SaveFormat.Read(bytes, content)` never throws and keeps today's order: size ('save too large'), JSON ('invalid JSON'), object, format tag ('wrong format tag'), then version. A version above current gives 'unsupported version X'; a version below current runs the upgrade steps in sequence. Then the collected value checks (at most 10 reasons, each at most 200 characters): kind, slot 1–10, savedAt finite, playerName, player personality valid (T2), unique character ids, affection and trust within −100..100, finite non-negative XP, and combat round ≥ 1, valid phase and status, fighters' stamina within 0..max, dice present and not all zero. (4) Upgrades: `SaveUpgrades` is an ordered list of steps (each from version n to n+1, working on the JSON object before mapping). The production list is empty because version 1 is the first; tests pass in a test-only step from a synthetic version 0. (5) Reconciliation: `SaveReconciler` pairs the saved state with the current content. Saved characters missing from the catalog are dropped; catalog characters missing from the save start with their starting affection and trust. The lineup is cleared if a member is gone, lacks combat stats, is duplicated, or the lineup size has changed. Reaction progress is kept even for absent ids, so it returns if the character comes back. A saved fight is restored as saved. The result is the GameState plus a `LoadReport` listing each adjustment.

tasks.technical_approach: Storage and slots in `AncientOrder.Rules.Saves`, plus the session's save operations. (1) `ISaveBackend` = `ReadAsync(key)` (bytes, or null when absent), `WriteAsync(key, bytes)`, `RemoveAsync(key)`, all returning `ValueTask`, with a CancellationToken. `FileSaveBackend(string folder)` stores each key as `{folder}/{key}.json`. It creates the folder on first write. It writes to `{key}.json.tmp`, flushes, then `File.Move(tmp, final, overwrite: true)`, so the old save survives any failure mid-write; a leftover .tmp is ignored and overwritten next time. It maps IOException disk-full results (ERROR_DISK_FULL, ERROR_HANDLE_DISK_FULL, ENOSPC) to STORAGE_ERROR 'Not enough storage space to save' and every other I/O or permission failure to STORAGE_ERROR 'Save storage is unavailable'. `MemorySaveBackend` serves tests and is the session's default. The rules never choose the folder: whatever runs them passes it in (Godot passes `user://saves`, T13). (2) `SaveStore` (port of saveStore.ts) over a backend and the content. Keys are `manual-01`…`manual-10`, with `auto-…` reserved. Operations: `SaveAsync(slot, game)`, `LoadAsync(slot)` (SAVE_NOT_FOUND 'No save found in slot X.'; damaged gives VALIDATION_ERROR 'Save file in slot X is corrupted: …'), `ListAsync()` (all ten slots: slot, exists, status empty/saved/corrupted, metadata slot/savedAt/playerName; a damaged slot has exists = false), `DeleteAsync(slot)` (SAVE_NOT_FOUND when empty; damaged slots can be deleted). Invalid slots give INVALID_SLOT 'Invalid slot number: X. Must be between 1 and 10.'. (3) Session operations on T9's GameSession, returning `ValueTask<Result<T>>`: SaveToSlot (slot check 'Slot must be an integer between 1 and 10', then GAME_NOT_FOUND, then save; returns slot, timestamp, playerName); LoadFromSlot (slot check, load; on success commits a fresh session snapshot with the loaded game, clearing pending orders and the last outcome, and returns the load report); ListSlots; DeleteSlot (returns slot and deleted = true).
